newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev ends weaker on pending peg, rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev ends weaker on pending peg, rate cut.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 1,667-1,670 per dollar, down from the opening 1,658-1,665 to adjust to the upcoming currency board peg and a pending cut in the central bank main interest rate, dealers said.
"News that the central bank will cut its main rate triggered a rise in (foreign currency) demand to profit on the pending lev peg (at 1,000 per mark) ," one dealer said.

"It is reasonable to buy foreign currency, especially marks at rates up to 962-964 levs ahead of the peg because yield on lev-denominated instruments will fall next week under the new main rate," the dealer added.
The mark traded at 963-964 levs at the close. Local traders calculate the lev/mark exchange rate through the mark/dollar cross on international markets.
Dealers said the central bank advised them earlier on Thursday it will set its main interest rate at 47.28 percent annually from Monday, down from 48.72 percent now.
Central bank officials were unavailable to comment but an official statement is expected later on Thursday.
Bulgaria's parliament approved on final reading amendments to the central bank law on Thursday, paving the way for the introduction of a currency board system from July 1.
The lev will be pegged at 1,000 per mark as an anchor in the currency board arrangement also from July 1. -- Sofia Newsroom, 3592 911 88
